warnings.message: frontend: npm is not pinned for frontend, and npm 11.16.0 (with Node.js 24.18.0 in frontend/.nvmrc) runs dependency install scripts that allowScripts does not cover unless strict-allow-scripts is set, so depcurfew apply writes strict-allow-scripts=true; with it, in npm 12.0.0 and later the install fails instead of blocking the script with a warning
warnings.fix: Make every place listed here run npm 12.0.0 or later (npm install -g npm@12.0.0 before it installs packages), and depcurfew apply leaves strict-allow-scripts out; pinning npm in packageManager or devEngines does not change the npm they run. Until then, review the packages an install stops at and add them to installScripts.allow or installScripts.deny in depcurfew.json

warnings.message: frontend: npm 11.15.0 (installed in frontend/Dockerfile, line 3) runs every dependency install script and has no allow-list, so "deny" cannot be enforced there
warnings.fix: Install npm 11.16.0 or later before packages are installed there (npm install -g npm@11.16.0), or move to a Node.js release that comes with it; npm 12 blocks dependency scripts by default
